_status: DRAFT â€” CLINICALLY UNVERIFIED. Every entry requires sign-off by a licensed clinician before use in a shipped app. Do not treat any value here as final.

drugs.frequency_en: twice daily (0h and 8h on day 1, then morning/evening days 2-3)
drugs.referral_trigger_text: Severe malaria (altered consciousness, severe anemia, jaundice, respiratory distress): refer for IV artesunate.
drugs.source_name: WHO Malaria Treatment Guidelines / Ethiopia National Malaria Guideline
drugs.source_detail: Standard 6-dose regimen over 3 days. Adult weight bands same as pediatric for this drug.

drugs.notes:
IV artesunate for severe malaria. Give IV (preferred) or IM. Always follow with full 3-day oral ACT once patient can tolerate oral.

Weight-based dosing:
â€¢ <20kg: 3.0 mg/kg per dose
â€¢ â‰¥20kg: 2.4 mg/kg per dose

Vials needed per dose:
â€¢ â‰¤25kg: 1 vial
â€¢ 26-50kg: 2 vials
â€¢ 51-75kg: 3 vials
â€¢ 76-100kg: 4 vials
drugs.referral_trigger_text: Below 5kg: refer immediately for specialist care.
drugs.iv_info:
[conc:20]Reconstitute:
1. Add 3ml of provided arginine/NaHCOâ‚ƒ solvent to 60mg artesunate vial
2. Shake gently until clear (~1 min)
3. Final concentration = 20mg/ml â†’ draw [ml]ml

Give slow IV over 1-2 min (do NOT further dilute for IV push).
Use within 1 hour of reconstitution.

Always follow with full 3-day oral ACT once patient can swallow.
Monitor Hb weekly for 4 weeks for post-artesunate delayed hemolysis (PADH).
drugs.safety_warning: Monitor for post-artesunate delayed hemolysis (PADH) â€” check Hb weekly for 4 weeks after treatment.
drugs.source_detail: â‰¥20kg: 2.4mg/kg at 0, 12, 24h. Reconstitute with 3ml solvent = 20mg/ml.

drugs.notes: Used for P. vivax malaria (with Primaquine). Adult dose capped at 600mg base total.
drugs.source_detail: 25mg base/kg total over 3 days (10/10/5mg/kg). Adult max 600mg base per dose on days 1-2.

drugs.safety_warning: Primaquine can cause dangerous hemolysis in patients with G6PD deficiency. VERIFY current Ethiopian protocol on G6PD testing requirement before dosing at this facility level.
drugs.source_name: Ethiopia national low-dose radical cure protocol (rolled out nationally 2018)
drugs.source_detail: 0.25mg/kg/day for 14 days. Adult dosing same as pediatric.

drugs.source_name: WHO pneumonia treatment guideline / Ethiopia STG
drugs.source_detail: 40mg/kg/dose BID for adults. Max 3g/day. Capsule formulations available for adult patients.

drugs.notes: For severe pneumonia not responding to oral antibiotics or unable to take oral. Administer IV over 30 minutes.
drugs.referral_trigger_text: Signs of severe respiratory distress: refer for higher-level care.
drugs.iv_info:
Reconstitute:
â€¢ 1g vial + 9.6ml sterile water = 100mg/ml â†’ draw [ml]ml

Infuse over 30 min.
Do NOT use calcium-containing fluids (Ringer's, Hartmann's).
drugs.source_detail: 50-100mg/kg/day divided q12h. Max 4g/day.
500mg day 1, 250mg days 2-5. Tablet formulation for adults.

drugs.notes: Standard adult dose: 625mg (500mg/125mg) PO BID or 1g (875mg/125mg) PO BID for severe infections.
drugs.source_detail: 625mg PO BID for moderate, 1g PO BID for severe infections.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Augmentin 625mg (500mg/125mg) PO twice daily for 7-10 days

For severe tonsillitis or penicillin-allergy non-responders:
  Augmentin 625mg PO BID Ã— 10 days

For peritonsillar abscess or severe infection:
  Augmentin 1g (875mg/125mg) PO BID Ã— 10 days

Second-line after amoxicillin or in treatment failure.
drugs.notes: Augmentin for GAS tonsillitis when amoxicillin fails or for peritonsillar abscess. 10-day course needed for GAS eradication.
drugs.safety_warning: Take with food to reduce GI upset. Diarrhea common with higher doses. Use 10-day course for GAS eradication.
drugs.source_detail: 625mg PO BID or 1g PO BID for severe cases. 10-day course for GAS.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Augmentin 625mg (500mg/125mg) PO twice daily for 5-7 days

For severe sinusitis or amoxicillin failure:
  Augmentin 1g (875mg/125mg) PO BID Ã— 7-10 days

First-line when: penicillin failure, daycare attendance, recent antibiotic use, severe symptoms.

Duration: 5-7 days for uncomplicated, 7-10 days for severe/recurrent.
drugs.notes: Augmentin for sinusitis when amoxicillin is inadequate (treatment failure, severe presentation, or recent abx use).
drugs.safety_warning: Augmentin preferred over amoxicillin alone for: treatment failure after 3 days, recent abx use, severe presentation, daycare attendance.
drugs.source_detail: 625mg PO BID or 1g PO BID. Duration 5-10 days per severity.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Augmentin 625mg (500mg/125mg) PO twice daily for 5-7 days

For severe or refractory acute otitis media:
  Augmentin 1g (875mg/125mg) PO BID Ã— 7-10 days

Use when: amoxicillin failure after 48-72h, severe AOM, recent antibiotic use, or recurrent infections.
drugs.notes: Augmentin for otitis media when amoxicillin fails or for severe presentation. Effective against beta-lactamase-producing organisms.
drugs.safety_warning: Take with food. Use high dose (90mg/kg/day amoxicillin component) for resistant organisms.
drugs.source_detail: 625mg PO BID or 1g PO BID. Second-line after amoxicillin monotherapy failure.

drugs.dose_display_en:
WHO PLAN A â€” Some Dehydration:
Give ORS based on dehydration status (not weight alone)

Mild dehydration: 50ml/kg over 4 hours
Moderate dehydration: 75-100ml/kg over 4 hours

Severe dehydration â†’ IV therapy (PLAN C)

Encourage additional ORS as patient desires.
Continue breastfeeding/feeding.
Reassess after 4 hours.

If no signs of dehydration: give ORS to replace ongoing losses (10ml/kg per loose stool).
drugs.notes: ORS volume depends on dehydration status. For adults, encourage drinking freely â€” aim for 200-400ml per loose stool.
drugs.source_detail: Adult ORS: same formulation as pediatric. Volume based on dehydration assessment.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Zinc 20mg once daily for 14 days (adult dose)

Evidence suggests benefit in zinc-deficient populations.
Consider 20mg elemental zinc daily.
drugs.source_detail: Adult dose 20mg daily for 14 days. Evidence strongest in malnourished populations.

drugs.drug_name_en: Ringer's Lactate IV (Plan C â€” severe dehydration)
drugs.dose_display_en:
WHO PLAN C â€” Severe Dehydration (Adult)
Total: 100 ml/kg IV Ringer's Lactate

Step 1: 30 ml/kg IV over 30 minutes
Step 2: 70 ml/kg IV over 2.5 hours

Reassess every 15-30 minutes.
Give ORS 5ml/kg/hour once patient can drink.
OR: 1-2L NS/RL rapid IV then 200ml/hr until rehydrated.
drugs.notes: WHO Plan C for severe dehydration with diarrhea. Use Ringer's Lactate first line. Normal Saline if RL unavailable.
drugs.safety_warning: Reassess every 15-30 minutes during IV therapy. Monitor for signs of fluid overload (crackles, raised JVP).
drugs.source_name: WHO diarrhea management guidelines â€” Adult
drugs.source_detail: 100ml/kg total. Adult: 30ml/kg over 30min + 70ml/kg over 2.5hrs.

drugs.notes: For severe bacterial gastroenteritis / dysentery (Salmonella, Shigella). 2g daily divided q12h or single daily dose.
drugs.source_detail: 1-2g IV daily for severe dysentery.

drugs.notes: Adult max 1g per dose. Max 4g per day. Use lowest effective dose for shortest duration.
drugs.safety_warning: Do not exceed 4g per 24 hours. Risk of hepatotoxicity at higher doses. Avoid in severe liver disease.
drugs.source_detail: 500mg-1g PO q4-6h PRN. Max 4g/day.

drugs.notes: Standard adult dose: 400mg PO every 6-8 hours. Range 200-800mg/dose. Max 2.4g/day.
drugs.safety_warning: Avoid in dehydration, active peptic ulcer, renal impairment, or aspirin allergy. Caution in elderly.
drugs.source_detail: 400mg PO q6-8h PRN. Max 2.4g/day.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Cotrimoxazole 960mg (800mg/160mg) PO twice daily for 3-5 days

Or 2 tablets of 400mg/80mg strength twice daily

Duration: 3 days for uncomplicated, 5-7 days for complicated UTI.
drugs.notes: Check local resistance patterns. Cotrimoxazole resistance is rising â€” consider alternatives if no improvement in 48 hours.
drugs.safety_warning: Caution in G6PD deficiency, renal impairment, elderly, and sulfonamide allergy.
drugs.source_detail: 960mg (DS) PO BID. Duration 3-7 days per local guidelines.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Amoxicillin 500mg PO three times daily for 5-7 days

Or 1g PO twice daily.
drugs.notes: Increasing resistance in E. coli. Use only if local susceptibility confirmed or as second-line.
drugs.source_detail: 500mg PO TID or 1g PO BID for 5-7 days.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Ciprofloxacin 250-500mg PO twice daily for 3-7 days

Uncomplicated UTI: 250mg PO BID Ã— 3 days
Complicated UTI: 500mg PO BID Ã— 7-14 days

RESISTANCE WARNING: Increasing E. coli resistance to fluoroquinolones in Ethiopia. Use only if:
  - Local susceptibility confirmed (antibiotic sensitivity testing done)
  - Patient did not respond to first-line options (cotrimoxazole)
  - Pyelonephritis requiring broader gram-negative coverage

Not first-line for uncomplicated UTI due to resistance concerns.
Avoid in pregnancy.
drugs.notes: Fluoroquinolone for UTI. Resistance is rising significantly in Ethiopia. Reserve for confirmed sensitivity or pyelonephritis. Do NOT use as first-line.
drugs.safety_warning: RESISTANCE WARNING: Not first-line due to increasing E. coli resistance. Avoid in pregnancy and breastfeeding. Caution in elderly (tendon rupture risk, QT prolongation, CNS effects including confusion). Avoid with NSAIDs (CNS excitation risk).
drugs.source_name: WHO EML / Ethiopia STG â€” resistance advisory
drugs.source_detail: 250-500mg PO BID Ã— 3-14 days depending on severity. Do NOT use first-line. Reserve for confirmed sensitivity.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Ceftriaxone 1g IV/IM once daily for 5-7 days

Or 1g IV every 12 hours for severe/complicated UTI.

For uncomplicated: 1g single dose IM or IV may be sufficient per some guidelines.
drugs.iv_info:
Reconstitute:
â€¢ 1g vial + 3.6ml sterile water for IM = 250mg/ml
â€¢ 1g vial + 9.6ml sterile water for IV = 100mg/ml

Inject IM deep in gluteal muscle.
Infuse IV over 2-4 minutes or 30 min infusion.
drugs.source_detail: 1g IV/IM daily. 1-2g daily for severe infections.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Amoxicillin 500mg PO three times daily for 7-10 days

Or 1g PO twice daily.

Important: 10-day course for confirmed Group A Strep to prevent rheumatic fever.
drugs.duration_warning: IMPORTANT: 10-day duration for strep eradication â€” do NOT default to 5 days.
drugs.source_detail: 500mg PO TID Ã— 10 days for strep pharyngitis. 10 days critical for rheumatic fever prevention.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Azithromycin 500mg PO once daily for 3-5 days

Or 500mg on day 1, then 250mg days 2-5.

Penicillin-allergy alternative.
drugs.notes: Penicillin-allergy alternative
drugs.source_detail: 500mg day 1, 250mg days 2-5 for tonsillopharyngitis.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Acute asthma exacerbation:

Inhaler (MDI) with spacer:
  2-4 puffs (100mcg each) every 20 min for 1st hour
  Then 2-4 puffs every 3-4 hours as needed

Nebulized:
  5mg (1mL of 0.5% solution) in 3mL NS every 20 min Ã— 3 doses
  Then 5mg every 4-6 hours as needed

For COPD:
  Inhaler: 2 puffs (100-200mcg) q4-6h PRN
drugs.notes: First-line rescue bronchodilator for acute asthma and COPD exacerbations.
drugs.referral_trigger_text: Acute severe asthma: unable to speak in sentences, RR >30, SpO2 <90%, use of accessory muscles â€” refer urgently.
drugs.safety_warning: Tremor, tachycardia, and palpitations are common side effects. Use with caution in ischemic heart disease.
drugs.source_name: GINA Guidelines / Ethiopia STG for Asthma
drugs.source_detail: Adult: 2-4 puffs MDI via spacer PRN. Nebulized 5mg per dose for acute exacerbations.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Prednisolone 40-50mg PO once daily for 5-7 days

For acute exacerbation not responding to bronchodilators.
No taper needed for courses <7 days.
drugs.referral_trigger_text: Life-threatening asthma: silent chest, cyanosis, exhaustion, altered consciousness â€” refer immediately.
drugs.safety_warning: Short-term use generally safe. Monitor for hyperglycemia, especially in diabetic patients.
drugs.source_detail: 40-50mg PO daily Ã— 5-7 days for acute exacerbations. 1mg/kg/day commonly used.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Aminophylline IV (second-line â€” only if inadequate response to salbutamol + steroids):

Loading dose: 5mg/kg IV over 30 min (if not on oral theophylline)
Maintenance: 0.5-0.7 mg/kg/hour IV infusion

Monitoring required: Check pulse, BP, and signs of toxicity.

Therapeutic range: 10-20 mcg/mL (theophylline level).
drugs.notes: Second-line for severe refractory asthma. Narrow therapeutic window â€” toxicity risk is significant. Only use if salbutamol + prednisolone inadequate and referral not possible.
drugs.safety_warning: Narrow therapeutic window. Toxicity: tachyarrhythmias, seizures, vomiting. Reduce dose in heart failure, liver disease, and elderly. Monitor theophylline levels if available. Avoid with ciprofloxacin, cimetidine, and macrolides (increase levels).
drugs.source_name: GINA / BTS Guidelines â€” second-line acute asthma
drugs.source_detail: 5mg/kg loading (if no recent theophylline), then 0.5-0.7mg/kg/hr. Use only in severe refractory cases.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Hydrocortisone 100-200mg IV STAT (for acute severe asthma)

Dosing:
  Adults: 100mg IV stat, then 100mg IV q6h
  Or: 200mg IV stat for life-threatening asthma

Duration: 3-5 days (no taper needed for short courses)

Alternative if IV access problematic: hydrocortisone 100mg IM

When to use: acute severe/life-threatening asthma where PO prednisolone not possible (vomiting, unable to swallow, unconscious, ventilated).

Switch to oral prednisolone once patient can swallow.

Onset: 2-4 hours (IV). Equivalent to prednisolone 25mg = hydrocortisone 100mg.
drugs.notes: IV steroid for acute severe asthma exacerbation when oral prednisolone is not feasible. Not first-line â€” give PO prednisolone whenever possible (less invasive, similar efficacy). GINA 2024: PO prednisolone is as effective as IV hydrocortisone in most cases.
drugs.safety_warning: Short courses (â‰¤7 days) do not require taper. Monitor blood glucose in diabetic patients. May cause fluid retention, hyperglycemia, hypokalemia with prolonged use.
drugs.source_name: GINA 2024 / BTS/SIGN 2023 â€” acute severe asthma
drugs.source_detail: 100-200mg IV stat then q6h. For acute severe asthma when PO route unavailable. Switch to PO prednisolone ASAP.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Hydrochlorothiazide 12.5-25mg PO once daily

Start: 12.5mg daily
Titrate: 25mg daily if needed

Max: 50mg daily (higher doses offer little extra benefit with more side effects).

Take in the morning (morning diuresis).

Often combined with other agents (ACEi, ARB, CCB) as combination therapy.
drugs.notes: First-line thiazide diuretic for hypertension. Start low, go slow. Monitor electrolytes (K+, Na+).
drugs.safety_warning: Monitor K+ and Na+ levels (risk of hypokalemia, hyponatremia). Caution in gout (raises uric acid), diabetes (may raise glucose), and renal impairment.
drugs.source_name: WHO PEN protocol / Ethiopian HTN guideline / JNC 8
drugs.source_detail: First-line: 12.5-25mg daily. Max 50mg/day. Check electrolytes at follow-up.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Amlodipine 5 mg PO once daily

Start: 5 mg once daily
Max: 10 mg once daily

Titrate: increase from 5mg to 10mg after 2-4 weeks if BP not at target.

First-line CCB for hypertension â€” especially effective in African patients.
No lab monitoring required.
May be combined with HCTZ, ACE inhibitors, or ARBs.
drugs.notes: Calcium channel blocker. Well tolerated. No lab monitoring needed. Effective in African patients per ALLHAT trial.
drugs.safety_warning: Common: ankle edema, headache, flushing. Caution in heart failure with reduced EF. Avoid grapefruit juice.
drugs.source_name: WHO PEN protocol / Ethiopian HTN guideline / JNC 8 / ESC 2024
drugs.source_detail: First-line: 5-10mg daily. Amlodipine 5mg is starting dose; titrate to 10mg. First-line CCB for African patients per ALLHAT trial evidence.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Enalapril 5-10mg PO once daily

Start: 5mg daily
Titrate: 10-20mg daily if needed

Max: 40mg daily (usually divided BID at higher doses)
drugs.notes: ACE inhibitor. Particularly beneficial in diabetes, heart failure, and CKD with proteinuria.
drugs.safety_warning: Check K+ and creatinine before starting and after 1-2 weeks. Contraindicated in pregnancy (do not use if pregnancy possible). Common: dry cough, angioedema (rare but serious). Avoid or reduce dose in renal impairment.
drugs.source_name: WHO PEN protocol / Ethiopian HTN guideline / JNC 8
drugs.source_detail: 5-20mg daily. First-line in diabetic patients. Check renal function before start and 1-2 weeks after.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Methyldopa 250mg PO twice daily (for hypertensive urgency / second-line)

Start: 250mg BID
Titrate: 500mg BID if needed (max 2g/day)

Note: Preferred use in pregnancy (safest antihypertensive in pregnancy).

Not first-line for routine HTN due to side effect profile.
drugs.notes: Centrally acting agent. Not first-line for routine HTN. Used in pregnancy or when other agents contraindicated.
drugs.safety_warning: Sedation, dizziness, dry mouth, depression, orthostatic hypotension. May cause hemolytic anemia (rare). Monitor LFTs.
drugs.source_detail: 250-500mg PO BID. Preferred agent in pregnancy. Max 2g/day.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Nifedipine ER (extended-release) 20-30mg PO once daily

Start: 20mg ER once daily
Titrate: increase by 10mg every 2-4 weeks

Target: 30-60mg ER once daily
Max: 90mg ER once daily

Take at same time each day, do NOT crush or chew ER tablets.

Dihydropyridine CCB â€” alternative to amlodipine.
Particularly useful in patients with peripheral edema on amlodipine.
drugs.notes: Calcium channel blocker. Alternative to amlodipine for African patients. ER formulation is preferred â€” avoids rapid vasodilation/side effects of immediate-release.
drugs.safety_warning: Common: ankle edema, headache, dizziness, flushing. Only use ER (extended-release) formulations for routine HTN â€” immediate-release may cause reflex tachycardia. Caution in heart failure with reduced EF.
drugs.source_name: WHO PEN / Ethiopian HTN guideline / JNC 8
drugs.source_detail: 20-30mg ER PO once daily. Max 90mg/day. Alternative CCB for hypertension.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Metformin 500mg PO twice daily (with meals)

Start: 500mg once daily for 1 week (reduce GI side effects)
Titrate: increase by 500mg weekly to target 1g BID

Standard maintenance: 500mg BID or 1g BID

Max: 2.55g (3 tablets of 850mg) per day

Extended-release available: 500mg-2g once daily.
drugs.notes: First-line oral hypoglycemic for Type 2 Diabetes. Biguanide class. Does NOT cause hypoglycemia as monotherapy.
drugs.safety_warning: Contraindicated in eGFR <30 (risk of lactic acidosis). Stop if: severe infection, dehydration, surgery, contrast dye (hold 48h post). GI side effects (diarrhea, nausea) common â€” start low, go slow. Monitor B12 with long-term use.
drugs.source_name: WHO PEN protocol / Ethiopian DM guideline / ADA 2025
drugs.source_detail: First-line for T2DM. 500mg BID, titrate to 1g BID. Max 2.55g/day.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Gliclazide 80mg PO twice daily

Or Gliclazide MR 30mg once daily (modified release)

Start: 40-80mg daily
Titrate: up to 160mg BID (standard) or 120mg once daily (MR)

Max: 320mg/day (standard immediate release)
drugs.notes: Sulfonylurea. Second-line after metformin or if metformin contraindicated. Stimulates pancreatic insulin secretion.
drugs.safety_warning: CAUTION: Can cause hypoglycemia, especially in elderly, renal impairment, or missed meals. Educate patient on hypoglycemia symptoms. Weight gain possible.
drugs.source_detail: 80-320mg daily IR or 30-120mg MR daily. Second-line after metformin.

drugs.dose_display_en:
REGULAR INSULIN (SHORT-ACTING)

Used for: acute hyperglycemia, DKA (with IV fluids), pre-meal bolus coverage, pregnancy.

SC dosing:
  Starting dose: 0.1-0.2 units/kg before meals
  If on NPH + Regular regimen: 2/3 NPH + 1/3 Regular per dose

IV dosing (acute settings):
  Initial bolus: 0.1 units/kg IV
  Infusion: 0.05-0.1 units/kg/hr in NS
  Rate: 50 units Regular in 50mL NS = 1 unit/mL

Onset: 30 min (SC), Peak: 2-3 hours, Duration: 5-8 hours

Monitor glucose hourly when IV insulin running.

Must be given 30 min before meals when used for prandial coverage.
drugs.notes: Short-acting insulin. Clear solution (vs NPH which is cloudy). Used for DKA, pre-meal coverage, and acute glucose control. Can be given IV (only Regular insulin â€” never NPH).
drugs.safety_warning: HIGH-ALERT MEDICATION. Hypoglycemia risk. Only Regular insulin can be given IV. Verify insulin type before administration. Use insulin syringe (NOT TB syringe). Discard opened vial after 28 days.
drugs.source_name: WHO PEN / Ethiopian DM guideline / ADA 2025
drugs.source_detail: Short-acting regular insulin. Requires correct type identification. IV protocol: 0.1 units/kg bolus + 0.1 units/kg/hr infusion for DKA.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Insulin NPH â€” Starting regimen:

Total daily dose: 0.2-0.3 units/kg/day (T2DM)

Once-daily regimen:
  NPH 10 units SC at bedtime (or morning)
  Increase by 2 units every 3 days until fasting glucose <130mg/dL

Twice-daily regimen:
  2/3 dose AM, 1/3 dose PM

Assess: Fasting glucose to titrate. Check for hypoglycemia.
drugs.notes: Insulin for T2DM: when oral agents fail (HbA1c >9% or symptomatic hyperglycemia). NPH insulin is the most available in Ethiopian public sector.
drugs.safety_warning: HIGH-ALERT MEDICATION. Hypoglycemia risk. Patient must have glucometer and hypoglycemia education. Store in refrigerator (2-8Â°C). Do NOT freeze. Reduce dose in renal impairment.
drugs.source_name: WHO PEN protocol / Ethiopian DM guideline / ADA 2025
drugs.source_detail: Start with 0.2-0.3 IU/kg/day NPH. Tirate to fasting glucose target. NPH most available in Ethiopia.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Omeprazole 20mg PO once daily

For dyspepsia/GERD:
  20mg once daily before breakfast Ã— 4-8 weeks

For H. pylori eradication (triple therapy):
  20mg BID + amoxicillin 1g BID + clarithromycin 500mg BID Ã— 14 days

For gastric ulcer:
  20-40mg once daily Ã— 4-8 weeks
drugs.notes: Proton Pump Inhibitor (PPI). First-line for dyspepsia, GERD, and peptic ulcer disease.
drugs.safety_warning: Long-term use (>1 year) associated with B12 deficiency, osteoporosis risk, GI infections (C. diff), hypomagnesemia. Use lowest effective dose for shortest duration.
drugs.source_name: Ethiopia STG / WHO EML / ACG guidelines
drugs.source_detail: 20mg daily for dyspepsia. 40mg for severe esophagitis or H. pylori therapy component.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Pantoprazole 40mg PO once daily

For dyspepsia/GERD:
  40mg once daily before breakfast Ã— 4-8 weeks

For severe GERD/esophagitis:
  40mg BID Ã— 8 weeks, then 40mg daily maintenance

IV option (when patient NPO):
  40mg IV once daily over 2-15 min

Alternative PPI to omeprazole. May have fewer drug interactions than omeprazole.
drugs.notes: Proton Pump Inhibitor (PPI). Alternative to omeprazole. Fewer CYP450 interactions than omeprazole â€” preferred when patient is on multiple meds (clopidogrel, warfarin, etc.).
drugs.safety_warning: Long-term use (>1 year) associated with B12 deficiency, osteoporosis risk, GI infections, hypomagnesemia. Use lowest effective dose for shortest duration.
drugs.source_name: Ethiopia STG / WHO EML / ACG guidelines
drugs.source_detail: 40mg PO once daily for dyspepsia/GERD. Alternative PPI with fewer drug interactions.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Ranitidine 150mg PO twice daily

For dyspepsia/GERD:
  150mg BID Ã— 4-8 weeks

For maintenance:
  150mg once daily at bedtime
drugs.notes: H2 receptor antagonist. Second-line after PPIs. Now less preferred due to NDMA impurity concerns in some formulations.
drugs.safety_warning: Less effective than PPIs. May cause confusion in elderly. Check for drug interactions (warfarin, theophylline, phenytoin).
drugs.source_detail: 150mg PO BID or 300mg at bedtime.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Antacid 10-20ml PO as needed for symptom relief

Or 1-2 tablets chewed 1 hour after meals and at bedtime.

Maximum: do not exceed 8 doses per 24 hours.

For mild, intermittent dyspepsia only. Not for chronic treatment.
drugs.notes: Over-the-counter option for mild intermittent symptoms. Provides rapid but short-lived relief.
drugs.safety_warning: May interfere with absorption of other drugs (tetracyclines, iron, digoxin, thyroxine, fluoroquinolones). Take 2 hours apart from other medications. Caution in renal impairment (magnesium toxicity).
drugs.source_detail: Symptom relief only. Not for long-term management of dyspepsia or GERD.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Cloxacillin 500mg PO four times daily (6-hourly) for 5-7 days

For cellulitis: 500mg-1g PO QID Ã— 5-7 days.

Max: 4g/day.

Take on empty stomach (1 hour before or 2 hours after meals).
drugs.notes: Antistaphylococcal penicillin. First-line for skin infections (impetigo, cellulitis, abscess).
drugs.source_detail: 500mg PO QID for skin/soft tissue infections. 1g PO QID for severe cellulitis.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Amoxicillin 500mg PO three times daily for 5-7 days

Less effective for Staph. Consider cloxacillin first if Staph suspected.
drugs.source_detail: 500mg PO TID. Second-line for skin infections.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Ceftriaxone 2g IV once daily for 7-14 days

Or 1g IV every 12 hours.

Duration:
  Uncomplicated: 7-10 days
  Severe: 10-14 days

First-line for severe typhoid or if quinolone resistance suspected.
drugs.notes: Third-generation cephalosporin. First-line for severe typhoid fever given increasing fluoroquinolone resistance. Effective against Salmonella typhi.
drugs.iv_info:
Reconstitute:
â€¢ 1g vial + 9.6ml sterile water = 100mg/ml

Infuse over 30 minutes.
For IM: 1g + 3.6ml lidocaine 1% or sterile water.
drugs.source_name: WHO Guidelines for Typhoid Fever / Ethiopia STG
drugs.source_detail: 2g IV daily Ã— 7-14 days. First-line for severe typhoid due to resistance patterns.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Azithromycin 500mg PO once daily for 7 days

Or 1g single dose for uncomplicated.

Effective alternative for uncomplicated typhoid.
Particularly useful when fluoroquinolone resistance suspected.

Safe in pregnancy.
drugs.source_detail: 500mg PO daily Ã— 7 days for uncomplicated typhoid. Alternative if ceftriaxone not available.

drugs.source_detail: 500mg PO BID Ã— 7-10 days. Resistance increasing â€” use with caution.

drugs.dose_display_en:
IV FLUIDS FOR HYPEREMESIS GRAVIDARUM

For mild-moderate dehydration:
  Normal Saline or Ringer's Lactate 1L IV over 2-4 hours

For severe dehydration:
  Bolus 500mL-1L NS over 30-60 min, then 125-150 mL/hr

Maintenance:
  D5 0.45% NaCl + KCl 20 mEq/L at 125 mL/hr
  Or continue NS/RL at 100-125 mL/hr

Add IV thiamine (100mg) before dextrose to prevent Wernicke's encephalopathy.

Monitor: Input/output, urine ketones, electrolytes, daily weight.
drugs.notes: IV fluids are the cornerstone of hyperemesis management. Correct dehydration BEFORE giving antiemetics. ALWAYS give thiamine before dextrose-containing fluids.
drugs.safety_warning: Give IV thiamine 100mg BEFORE any dextrose-containing fluids (risk of Wernicke's encephalopathy). Monitor for fluid overload. Check electrolytes daily.
drugs.source_detail: NS or RL for rehydration. Add thiamine before dextrose. Monitor electrolytes and urine output.

drugs.dose_display_en:

drugs.source_detail: 75mg IM/IV single dose. NSAIDs are first-line for acute renal colic.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Hyoscine Butylbromide 20mg IM/IV

Or 10-20mg PO three times daily.

Antispasmodic â€” relaxes ureteral smooth muscle.

May be combined with diclofenac for added effect.

drugs.dose_display_en:
DIABETIC KETOACIDOSIS â€” MANAGEMENT PROTOCOL

1. IV FLUIDS (CORRECT DEFICIT FIRST)
   â€¢ NS 1L over 1 hour (first hour)
   â€¢ NS 1L over 2 hours (second hour)
   â€¢ NS 1L over 4 hours (hours 3-6)
   â€¢ NS 1L over 6 hours (hours 7-12)
   Total: ~4-6L deficit in first 24h

   When glucose <250 mg/dL (14 mmol/L): switch to D5 0.45% NaCl

2. INSULIN (REGULAR IV ONLY â€” never NPH)
   â€¢ Bolus: 0.1 units/kg Regular IV (optional; many protocols skip bolus)
   â€¢ Infusion: 0.1 units/kg/hr Regular IV (50 units in 50mL NS = 1 unit/mL)
   â€¢ Target: decrease glucose by 50-75 mg/dL/hr
   â€¢ When glucose <250 mg/dL: decrease insulin to 0.05 units/kg/hr
     and add dextrose to fluids

3. POTASSIUM
   â€¢ If K+ <3.3 mEq/L: hold insulin, give 20-30 mEq K+/hr
   â€¢ If K+ 3.3-5.3 mEq/L: give 20-30 mEq K+/L in IV fluids
   â€¢ If K+ >5.3 mEq/L: hold K+, recheck in 2h

4. BICARBONATE
   â€¢ NOT routinely recommended
   â€¢ Consider only if pH <6.9 (give 50-100 mEq NaHCOâ‚ƒ in 200mL D5W over 1h)

5. MONITORING (hourly until stable)
   â€¢ Glucose (at bedside)
   â€¢ Electrolytes (K+, Na+) every 2-4 hours
   â€¢ Venous pH / bicarbonate every 4 hours
   â€¢ I/O chart â€” target urine output >0.5 mL/kg/hr

6. TRANSITION TO SC INSULIN
   â€¢ When: glucose <200 mg/dL, pH â‰¥7.3, bicarbonate â‰¥15, patient tolerating oral
   â€¢ Overlap: start SC insulin 1-2 hours BEFORE stopping IV insulin
   â€¢ SC regimen: calculate total daily dose (0.5-0.6 units/kg), give 2/3 in AM, 1/3 in PM

CALL FOR HELP IF:
  â€¢ Glucose not decreasing after 4 hours
  â€¢ K+ <3.0 or >6.0 mEq/L
  â€¢ pH remains <7.0 after 6 hours
  â€¢ Altered consciousness or hypotension
drugs.notes: DKA is a MEDICAL EMERGENCY. This protocol assumes adult DKA. For children, use pediatric-specific DKA protocol. CBC, BMP, VBG, and urine ketones should be sent stat upon presentation.
drugs.safety_warning: Do NOT use NPH insulin IV. Only Regular insulin can be given IV. Monitor glucose hourly â€” risk of hypoglycemia if IV fluids changed without adjusting insulin rate. Cerebral edema (rare in adults, more common in children). Watch for hypokalemia when insulin is started.
drugs.source_name: ADA / Joint British Diabetes Societies (JBDS) / Ethiopian DM guideline
drugs.source_detail: Comprehensive DKA protocol: Fluids â†’ Insulin â†’ K+ â†’ Bicarb. Regular insulin IV only. Transition protocol included.
